newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko threatens to go back on Belarus deal.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko threatens to go back on Belarus deal.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko, facing a deadlock between supporters and opponents in parliament late on Friday, threatened to go back on a Russia-brokered peace deal designed to end the political crisis in Belarus.
"If you do not pass this resolution into law, I will be forced to return to the situation as it was the day before yesterday," Lukashenko told deputies.

Parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky, who signed the deal along with Lukashenko and constitutional court chief Valery Tikhinya at dawn, accused Lukashenko of lying after the president complained that he had promised to make sure the deal was approved by the end of Friday's session.
The deal ran into trouble straight away when deputies dismissed it as a sell-out and failed to pass it three times.
Lukashenko wants a two-thirds majority of 132 deputies to approve the deal, making it constitutionally binding. But opposition deputies want to merely approve it with a simple majority of 100.
They are worried Lukashenko will be able to push through significantly wider powers for himself despite the agreement, brokered by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
